jobs.occupation: Doctoral researcher (m/f/d/x) in microbial systems biophysics (Biophysiker/in)
jobs.description: Founded in 1409, Leipzig University is one of Germany’s largest universities and a leader in research and medical training. With around 30,000 students and more than 5000 members of staff across 14 faculties, it is at the heart of the vibrant and outward-looking city of Leipzig. Leipzig University offers an innovative and international working environment as well as an exciting range of career opportunities in research, teaching, knowledge and technology transfer, infrastructure and administration.The Division of Systems Biophysics of Microbial Dynamics at the Peter Debye Institute for Soft Matter Physics at the Faculty of Physics and Earth System Sciences, seeks to fill the above position.About the position- Salary group 13 TV-L - Fixed-term position in accordance with the training plan, initially for 1 year; an extension of the fixed-term contract is planned- 50 % of a full-time position- As soon as possibleThe newly formed Division of Systems Biophysics of Microbial Dynamics (https://home.uni-leipzig.de/sysbiophys/) , led by Professor Katja Taute, is part of the Peter Debye Institute for Soft Matter Physics (https://www.physes.uni-leipzig.de/en/pdi) , which hosts a broad range of biophysics research. Active matter, including bacterial systems, is a growing key research area at the Institute. Our research group develops and uses biophysical methods, including high-throughput, 3D bacterial tracking and microfluidics, in combination with theory and simulations, to quantitatively analyse the spatio-temporal dynamics of bacteria at the level of individuals and populations. One research focus is the chemotactic navigation of bacteria in mechanically complex environments. In nature, swimming bacteria navigate relative to chemical stimuli in environments ranging from open waters to soil and the gut.The new doctoral researcher is to investigate how the gut bacterium E. coli navigates mechanically complex environments that mimic properties of its natural habitat. Properties of both the bacteria and the environment will be modulated in a controlled fashion to identify the underlying physical mechanisms and address the following questions:- What is the relationship between behavioural and material parameters that enable optimal navigation?- Is optimal intracellular information processing specific to the type of environment?- How do bacteria navigate mechanical gradients?The role- Independent, original, experimental scientific research on the above project- Additional scientific qualification (preparing a doctoral thesis)- Thorough documentation of research- Publication of research results, for example at conferences, workshops, or in scientific articles- Contributions to the Institute’s teaching responsibilitiesAbout you- An excellent scientific university degree (master of science or comparable) in (bio-)physics, (bio-)engineering or a related field- Very good command of at least one programming language (Matlab or Python preferred) and of quantitative scientific data analysis- A track record of academic excellence (e.g. very good grades in the course of study, research or study scholarships and prizes, scientific publications)- Written and spoken professional fluency in English (at least equivalent to level B2)- Excellent written communication skills, demonstrated through coherent, structured and precise writing- Experience with microscopy and scientific image processing would be an advantage- Interest in quantitative experimental interdisciplinary science- Collaborative mindset and teamwork skillsWhat we offer you- a varied role with a high degree of responsibility in the dynamic environment of a major university- a professional English-language work environment at the leading edge of interdisciplinary science- Collaboration in a friendly, supportive and motivated team- flexible working hours and mobile working to support work-life balance- Goal-oriented staff development throughout your working life, with opportunities for continuing professional development- a wide range of occupational health management services - Remuneration in line with the collective bargaining agreement of the federal states (TV-L), including an annual special payment and occupational pension scheme- excellent transport links and the option to purchase a discounted public transport ticket, such as the Deutschlandticket as a commuter pass- a wide range of food options in the refectories and cafés operated by Studentenwerk Leipzig.Leipzig University aims to increase the proportion of women in positions of responsibility and therefore expressly invites qualified women to apply. Severely disabled persons – or persons deemed legally equal to them under Book IX of the German Social Code – are encouraged to apply and will be given preference in the case of equal suitability. If you have any questions about accessibility or need assistance with this application process, please contact Leipzig University’s disability officers at: schwerbehindertenvertretung@uni-leipzig.de (https://mailto:schwerbehindertenvertretung@uni-leipzig.de) .Have we sparked your interest?Please submit your application in English addressed to Fakultät für Physik und Erdsystemwissenschaften, Herrn Dekan Professor Dr. Johannes Quaas by 1 November 2026 via our online application portal.Please include the following documents with your application:- A short letter of motivation (max. 1 page) in which you clearly explain why you would like to work on this project- A scientific CV (evidence of creative and independent scientific work is an advantage)- The names and contact information of two people who have agreed to provide academic references- Academic transcripts clearly listing the courses taken and grades achieved in your entire scientific higher education (bachelor’s as well as master’s or comparable degrees)

We are looking to support our rapidly growing team as soon as possible: Postdoctoral Fellow in Computational Cancer Evolution (f/m/x)Department I of Internal Medicine - CECADYour tasksWe are looking for an ambitious postdoctoral researcher with a proven track record in computational cancer evolution to join our Integrated Cancer Research Laboratory at the CECAD Research Center in Cologne. In this role, you will reconstruct the clonal and subclonal architecture of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and track its evolution under targeted therapies. Using bulk and single-cell sequencing data, you will infer tumour phylogenies and quantify intratumour heterogeneity, subclonal selection and genomic instability (e.g. copy-number alterations, whole-genome doubling and chromothripsis).You will identify evolutionary trajectories leading to treatment resistance, relapse and Richter transformation. Furthermore, you will develop and apply computational methods based on evolutionary principles and integrate genomic, transcriptomic and spatial data with clinical outcomes. Your analyses will link evolutionary features to treatment response, MRD kinetics and survival.For this work, the lab has access to blood and bone marrow samples from more than 900 patients with CLL treated within prospective clinical trials of the German CLL Study Group (GCLLSG), including samples taken before treatment and at relapse, linked to detailed clinical and measurable residual disease (MRD) data.You will lead your own projects, contribute to collaborative projects within the lab and with external partners, and co-supervise PhD and Master students.Your profile• A PhD in bioinformatics, computational biology, statistics, physics, computer science or a related field• A proven track record in computational cancer evolution, demonstrated by first-author publications• Hands-on experience in reconstructing clonal and subclonal tumour evolution from sequencing data (e.g. clonal deconvolution, phylogenetic inference, mutational signatures)• Experience in copy-number and structural variant analysis from whole-genome or whole-exome sequencing data; experience with single-cell DNA or RNA sequencing data is a plus• Fluency in Python and/or R, and experience with reproducible workflows (e.g. Snakemake, Nextflow) on high performance computing clusters• Experience with longitudinal or clinical trial data and with haematological malignancies is a plus• Ability to work independently and in close collaboration with clinicians and wet-lab scientists• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spokenOur offer• Everything but ordinary: You can expect a secure job in a challenging, innovative environment – including company pension schemes and regular working hours without business trips.• Work-life balance: Whether full-time or part-time, with or without children – with numerous support options, we will find the right path together.• Team spirit in R(h)ine culture: You will be warmly welcomed by an interdisciplinary team that values mutual respect and helpfulness.• Strong perspectives: We offer extensive training opportunities – so you can continuously grow and set new goals.Your future in detailThe Integrated Cancer Research Laboratory (www.al-sawaf-lab.com), led by Prof Othman Al-Sawaf and based at the CECAD and Department I of Internal Medicine, was founded in 2024 and is funded by a large Emmy-Noether-Grant of the German Research Council (DFG). The focus of the lab is to integrate multimodal analyses to study the plasticity, evolution and prognosis of cancer with a special focus on hematological malignancies. To this end, the lab utilizes a unique biobank with blood and bone marrow samples from patients treated within large (>900 patients) prospective clinical trials. The group is embedded in a network with many local collaborators, including the Collaborative Research Center (CRC) 1530 and the German CLL Study Group (GCLLSG), as well as many national and international partners in academia and industry. Previous work has been frequently cited (Al-Sawaf et al, N Engl J Med 2025; Al-Sawaf et al, Nature Medicine 2024; Al-Sawaf et al, Nature Medicine 2023; see Pubmed) and the aim of the lab is to continue producing highly impactful and patient-relevant results.ContactProf. Dr. Othman Al-SawafTel: +49 221 478-84816Universitätsklinikum Köln AöRGeschäftsbereich PersonalKerpener Str. 6250937 KölnUniklinik Köln Karriere Application deadline: 29 November 2026Job-ID: 3ftptfctWe look forward to receiving your application and getting to know you!

With more than 1.300 employees, it is the largest of the university's 14 faculties and provides training for approximately 3,500 students in human medicine and dentistry as well as pharmacy and midwifery. The Faculty of Medicine was founded in 1415, making it one of the oldest medical faculties in Germany with an unbroken tradition of teaching.PhD Position - Craniofacial Biology and PTEN-Dependent Tissue HomeostasisThe research group "Cranio- and Orofacial Development" (https://research.uni-leipzig.de/petersen_lab/) at Leipzig University Medical Center (UKL) offers a PhD position within a DFG-funded collaborative project investigating PTEN-dependent craniofacial tissue homeostasis. The project is particularly suited to candidates interested in craniofacial and skeletal biology, molecular signaling, spatial omics, and metabolism.Project BackgroundPTEN is a central regulator of PI3K-AKT signaling and coordinates cell growth, metabolism, and tissue homeostasis. The project investigates how loss of PTEN in the osteoblast lineage alters the postnatal craniofacial complex. The PhD project will focus on teeth and their supporting periodontal tissues, alveolar and craniofacial bone, and the temporomandibular joint (TMJ). Using an inducible postnatal genetic mouse model, we aim to determine how PTEN-dependent signaling changes tissue architecture, bone remodeling, cellular states, and molecular programs. A complementary part of the project will investigate the associated adipose/metabolic phenotype in close collaboration with Dr. Antje Garten and her group from the Molecular Endocrinology at the Center for Pediatric Research (https://research.uni-leipzig.de/garten_lab/).The PhD candidate will investigate- PTEN-dependent changes in teeth and periodontal tissues, craniofacial and alveolar bone, and the TMJ- Cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying altered bone remodeling and craniofacial tissue homeostasis after postnatal PTEN deletion- Spatially resolved tissue responses and their relationship to PTEN-associated adipose/metabolic changesMethods and ApproachesThe project combines state-of-the-art experimental and computational techniques, including:- Inducible transgenic mouse models and genetic reporter systems- Histology, immunofluorescence, advanced microscopy, and micro-computed tomography- Spatial transcriptomics of dental, periodontal, bone, and TMJ tissues- Molecular biology, quantitative image analysis, proteomic integration, and bioinformatic analysesCandidate ProfileWe are looking for a highly motivated candidate with:- Master of Science degree or a Diploma in Biology, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Bioinformatics or Chemistry- Interest in craniofacial biology, mechanobiology, or regenerative medicine- Experience in molecular biology, cell biology, animal models, and/or bioinformatics- Strong motivation to work in an international and interdisciplinary research environment- Good communication skills and proficiency in EnglishResearch EnvironmentThe project is embedded in the Department of Orthodontics at Leipzig University Medical Center. Our research focuses on craniofacial biology, tooth and periodontal tissue homeostasis, skeletal remodeling, genetic mouse models, advanced imaging, and spatial omics. The collaboration with Dr. Antje Garten provides complementary expertise in PTEN biology, metabolism, and adipose tissue, enabling the PhD candidate to connect local craniofacial phenotypes with systemic metabolic alterations.Institution: Department für Kopf- und Zahnmedizin, Poliklinik für KieferorthopädieType of employment: Fixed-term position for 3 years (third-party funded)Working Hours: part-time (26,00h)Start date: 01.12.2026Remuneration: TV-L 13- A fully funded PhD position (3 years)- Participation in an international research collaboration- Access to cutting-edge technologies, including spatial transcriptomics and advanced imaging- A dynamic and collaborative research environment- Opportunities for international exchange and conference participationHow to applyPlease apply with a single PDF containing a cover letter describing your previous research experience and motivation to join our lab; curriculum vitae; copies of relevant qualifications (degree, diploma and, if applicable, animal-course certificates); and the contact details of two refereesApply now for this position via our applicant portal by 31 October 2026 .Your contact personFor further information about the application process, please contact Dr. Julian Petersen (E: Julian.Petersen@medizin.uni-leipzig.de).Applicants with severe disabilities will be given preferential consideration if equally qualified. Please include relevant supporting documentation with your application.Please note that, due to legal requirements, we can only employ applicants who are immune to measles. You will be required to provide the relevant proof of immunity.For information on data protection, please visit: Data protection
